about.text: I'm a Full-Stack & AI Engineer based in South Korea. I design and build web services end to end, from Next.js and TypeScript frontends to NestJS, GraphQL and MongoDB backends, deployed with Docker and NGINX. I don't treat full-stack and AI separately: I connect them inside one working service.

hero.text: I'm Azamjon — a Full-Stack & AI Engineer based in South Korea. I build web services end to end and connect them with AI to solve real business problems.

who.story1: I grew up in Uzbekistan and studied engineering. What pulled me in was never the theory, but the moment a real problem finally gets solved. Software turned out to be the fastest way to keep having that moment, so I started building, and I never stopped.
who.story2: Today I work across full-stack development and AI. Alongside it, I'm doing a master's in finance, because I want to understand not only how products are built, but why they matter to the people and businesses using them.
who.nextText: To keep growing as an engineer, and to build and take part in projects that make a real difference for people.
who.photoAlt: Azamjon smiling in a warmly lit café

hero.fullstackText: Web apps from the first screen to the database: *typed frontends*, *GraphQL APIs* and clean data models.

hero.devopsText: *Docker* environments and *Linux VPS* deployments behind NGINX, with PM2 and SSL.
hero.realtimeText: *Live chat* over WebSocket, *OAuth* sign-in with Google, Apple and Kakao, JWT with refresh tokens and _TOTP 2FA_.

expertise.backendText: *NestJS / GraphQL* and *Express REST* APIs on MongoDB, a server-rendered _EJS admin_, OAuth and token auth.
expertise.aiText: Fine-tuned *PyTorch image classifiers* served through FastAPI, and Gemini analysis inside _real products_.
expertise.devopsText: *Docker* environments and *Ubuntu VPS* deployments behind NGINX, kept running with PM2 and SSL.

workflow.intro: How I take a product from the *first question* to a _running service_, and the tools I use every day.
workflow.planText: Understand the business problem, then shape the scope, *data models* and architecture.
workflow.developText: Typed *Next.js* frontends and *NestJS / GraphQL* APIs, built in small steps with Git.
workflow.testText: *Jest and Supertest* specs for auth flows, APIs checked in Postman, models scored on a _held-out test set_.

workflow.iterateText: Harden what real use breaks: a *rule-based fallback* when Gemini fails, polling when WebSocket drops.

tldr: What|A marketplace connecting customers with *verified technicians* for iPhone, MacBook, iPad and Apple Watch repairs.
My role|Built *solo*: product, UI, backend, AI integration and DevOps.
Stack|Next.js, NestJS, GraphQL, MongoDB, WebSocket, Gemini, Docker.
Scale of the build|*2* backend services, *20* feature modules, *3* user roles, *16* test suites.
fixora.problem: Finding a *trusted, nearby* Apple technician is slow, and booking, payment and communication are scattered across calls and chats.
fixora.solution: One platform that *matches, books, chats and tracks* the repair from the first message to the review.
roles: Customer|Describe the issue, compare technicians, book, pay a deposit, *chat in real time* and leave a review.
Technician|*6-step onboarding* and verification (Pending → Under review → Approved), then accept jobs, update status, publish articles and 24-hour stories.
Admin|Verify technicians, monitor bookings, payments and disputes, track KPIs and get *Telegram alerts*.
fixora.ruleDeposit: No paid deposit → the job can’t start.
fixora.rulePhone: The phone number is revealed only after the booking is accepted.
fixora.aiNote: AI recommends: it never auto-assigns a technician.
fixora.searchAlt: Fixora technician search with filters and a map
fixora.realtime: Every booking has its own *WebSocket chat*, saved to the database, with a _polling fallback_ when the socket drops.
fixora.signinAlt: Fixora sign-in screen with Google and Kakao
fixora.channelsRetry: Failed deliveries are retried every 5 minutes.
fixora.archData: MongoDB · Gemini API · Kakao Maps · notification pipeline
fixora.archInfra: Docker + NGINX on an Ubuntu VPS
decisions: Why GraphQL?|One *typed contract* for three role apps: customer, technician and admin.
Why hybrid AI?|An AI outage must *never stop a booking*: rule-based fallback takes over.
Why deposit-gated jobs?|Protects technicians from *no-shows* and fake bookings.
Why a pluggable payment gateway?|Swap the mock for KakaoPay *without a refactor* (adapter pattern).
fixora.decisionsNote: Every decision is logged with an ID in the repo.
challenges: *Multi-role complexity*: different features and permissions per role
*Real-time consistency* across chat, booking status and notifications
*AI reliability*: API downtime and low-confidence answers
*Payment provider limits*: KakaoPay integration and testing
nextSteps: Better matching with more signals and user feedback
Analytics: growth, conversion and repair trends
model: *Users* have role-specific profiles (customer, technician, admin, support staff) with verification status.
Every repair request is tied to a *Device* (brand, model, serial number, issue), so the history stays with it.
*Booking is the single source of truth*: status, parties, timestamps and a price snapshot; everything else references it.
*Payments* (deposit and final), *messages*, *reviews* and *notifications* all hang off the booking.
features: Kakao Maps|Nearby technicians with *distance and ETA*, on Korea’s most used map platform.
Smart search filters|Device type, specialty, location, rating, *online status*, response time and distance radius.
Booking chat|A chat inside every booking: share *photos, notes and estimates* without switching apps.
Live status updates|Job status and ETA *pushed live* over WebSocket to every connected device.
Reviews & ratings|Only after a *completed* booking, one review per booking, so ratings stay honest.
Articles & stories|Verified technicians publish articles and *24-hour stories* to build trust.

tldr: What|Upload a car photo → model, confidence, *Top-5 alternatives*, specs and a visual explanation.
My role|Built *solo*: data, training, evaluation, API, UI and deployment.
Stack|PyTorch, ConvNeXt-Tiny, FastAPI, Next.js, Docker, NGINX.
Result|*88.3%* Top-5 accuracy on 855 unseen test images, *~250 ms* per image.
carvia.problem: Identifying a car model from a photo is *harder than it looks*.
carvia.solutionLead: A fine-tuned vision model behind a simple API and web UI.
carvia.solution: From a *single photo* it returns the car model, a confidence score, Top-5 alternatives and key specifications, and says _Uncertain_ instead of guessing.
steps: Image input|Upload a photo or take one with the phone camera.
Preprocessing|Resize, normalize and convert to a tensor.
Response|Prediction, confidence, Top-5 and processing time (~250 ms).
carvia.resultAlt: CarVia result page: Porsche 911 with 72.7% confidence and specifications
carvia.dataLead: *5,466* images · *37* classes · *11* brands of the Korean market.
carvia.dataCaption: Every image was audited before training, so the test score is honest.
carvia.resultsNote: Measured on the 855-image test set the model never saw.
carvia.hardPairs: Hardest pairs: *Mercedes C / E / S-Class* and *BMW X3 / X5 / 5 Series*.
carvia.gateResult: *87.5%* of accepted answers are correct, with *67.7%* of photos accepted (validation set).
carvia.gateQuote: I traded a little coverage for answers people can trust: below the gate the app says _Uncertain_.
carvia.tempText: Fitted on validation data so the confidence *means something*: average confidence when the model is
explain: Grad-CAM heatmap|Shows *which part of the car* the model looked at.
Spec catalog|Body type, fuel, transmission, drivetrain, seats and a *short AI overview*.
Phone camera capture|Take a photo straight from the *rear camera* on mobile.
carvia.devicesAlt: CarVia upload screen on a laptop and a phone
challenges: Model confusion|Curated *37-class* dataset and a fine-tuned ConvNeXt-Tiny.
Dataset quality|Audit and curation: *no duplicates across splits*, no corrupt files.
Over-confident wrong answers|*Calibrated gate* (≥ 45% and ≥ 8%) plus temperature scaling.
Production serving|Dockerized FastAPI service with a */health* check.
Real-world variation|Augmentation tuned for *phone photos*: angles, light and crops.
carvia.archInfra: Docker · Docker Compose · Let’s Encrypt SSL · Ubuntu VPS · ~250 ms per image
carvia.archTraining: Trained locally on a GTX 1650 with mixed precision (FP16).
decisions: Why ConvNeXt-Tiny?|Strong accuracy that still runs *fast on a CPU VPS*.
Why a calibrated gate?|A wrong *confident* answer hurts trust more than “Uncertain”.
Why audit the dataset?|*No leakage* between splits means the test score is honest.
Why a separate FastAPI service?|The model stays *isolated* from the web app and scales on its own.
carvia.classesLead: Per-class F1 on the test set: the *five strongest* and the *five hardest* classes. Hover a bar for precision, recall and the number of test images.
carvia.classesNote: Three of the hardest classes have only *4–7 test images*, and most mistakes are *siblings of the same brand*. More data for those models is the next lever.
